## Functions

```{r functions}
# Weights -> tibble ----------------------------------------------------------

# Convert a named vector of gene weights into a tibble sorted by weight,
# with the rank of each gene (1 = highest weight)
weights_to_tibble <- function(weights) {
  sorted <- sort(weights, decreasing = TRUE)
  tibble::tibble(
    gene = names(sorted),
    rank = seq_along(sorted),
    weight = unname(sorted)
  )
}

# Cutoff methods -------------------------------------------------------------
# Every method returns the NUMBER of top genes to keep (N), so gene sets can
# be pulled the same way for every method with get_top_genes()

# Kneedle (offline, single knee):
#  - Use only positive weights, sorted from highest to lowest
#  - Scale x (rank) and y (weight) to [0, 1]
#  - The sorted curve is convex and decreasing, so the straight line from the
#    first point to the last point is y = 1 - x
#  - The elbow is the point where the curve sits farthest below that line,
#    i.e. where (1 - x) - y is largest
# NOTE: we don't smooth the curve or use a sensitivity parameter, since we
# only want one knee per curve. Here kneedle reduces to the max of the
# difference curve.
find_kneedle_n <- function(weights) {
  positive_weights <- sort(weights[weights > 0], decreasing = TRUE)
  n <- length(positive_weights)
  stopifnot("Need at least 3 positive weights to find an elbow" = n >= 3)

  x_norm <- (seq_len(n) - 1) / (n - 1)
  y_norm <- (positive_weights - min(positive_weights)) /
    (max(positive_weights) - min(positive_weights))

  difference_curve <- (1 - x_norm) - y_norm
  as.integer(unname(which.max(difference_curve)))
}

# Outlier detection with MAD:
#  - Median and MAD are taken over ALL genes (not just positive ones), so the
#    "background" is defined by the full gene distribution
#  - We only keep the upper tail, since we want genes with high weights
#  - stats::mad() uses the default constant (1.4826), so the MAD is on the same
#    scale as a standard deviation for normally distributed data
find_mad_cutoff <- function(weights, n_mads = 3) {
  mad_value <- stats::mad(weights)
  if (mad_value == 0) {
    warning("MAD is 0, so every gene above the median will be called an outlier.")
  }
  stats::median(weights) + n_mads * mad_value
}

find_log_mad_n <- function(weights, n_mads = 3) {
  log_weights <- log10(weights[weights > 0])
  cutoff <- stats::median(log_weights) + n_mads * stats::mad(log_weights)
  sum(log_weights > cutoff)
}

# Pull the top n genes by weight
# function to extract the top genes from each MP
# takes a list of named gene weight vectors and returns a list of gene id vectors,
# ordered by decreasing weight, with `num_genes` genes for each MP
extract_top_genes <- function(mp_list, num_genes){

  # get the top X number of genes for each MP
  mp_top_list <- mp_list |>
    purrr::map(function(weights){
      weights |>
        sort(decreasing = TRUE) |>
        head(n = num_genes) |>
        names() # return gene ids not weights
    })

  return(mp_top_list)
}

# Set similarity -------------------------------------------------------------

# Jaccard index; NA when both sets are empty (e.g., no significant pathways)
jaccard_index <- function(a, b) {
  union_size <- length(union(a, b))
  if (union_size == 0) return(NA_real_)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / union_size
}

# Overlap coefficient = |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|)
# Useful because the sets are nested (e.g., top_50 is always inside top_200).
# Jaccard is pulled down just by the size difference; overlap says whether
# the smaller set is contained in the larger one.
overlap_coefficient <- function(a, b) {
  min_size <- min(length(a), length(b))
  if (min_size == 0) return(NA_real_)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / min_size
}

# All pairwise similarities for a named list of sets
calculate_pairwise_similarity <- function(set_list, similarity_fn) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(set_1 = names(set_list), set_2 = names(set_list)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      value = purrr::map2_dbl(set_1, set_2, \(a, b) similarity_fn(set_list[[a]], set_list[[b]]))
    )
}

# Pairwise similarity within each group of a data frame
#  - group_col: column to compare within (e.g., "mp" to compare methods)
#  - name_col: column that names each set (e.g., "method")
#  - set_col: list column holding the sets
calculate_similarity_by_group <- function(df, group_col, name_col, set_col, similarity_fn) {
  df |>
    tidyr::nest(.by = dplyr::all_of(group_col)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(similarity = purrr::map(data, \(group_df) {
      set_list <- purrr::set_names(group_df[[set_col]], as.character(group_df[[name_col]]))
      calculate_pairwise_similarity(set_list, similarity_fn)
    })) |>
    dplyr::select(-data) |>
    tidyr::unnest(similarity)
}

# Heatmap of pairwise similarity, one facet per group
plot_similarity_heatmap <- function(similarity_df, facet_col, set_levels, fill_label, title) {
  similarity_df |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      set_1 = factor(set_1, levels = set_levels),
      set_2 = factor(set_2, levels = set_levels)
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(set_1, set_2, fill = value)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey90") +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[facet_col]])) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = fill_label, title = title) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

# ORA ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Hallmark ORA with clusterProfiler
# pvalueCutoff/qvalueCutoff are set to 1 so ALL tested pathways come back.
# We filter on p.adjust later, so we keep the full results.
run_hallmark_ora <- function(genes, universe, term2gene) {
  result <- clusterProfiler::enricher(
    gene = genes,
    universe = universe,
    TERM2GENE = term2gene,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    qvalueCutoff = 1
  )
  # enricher() returns NULL when no genes map to any gene set
  if (is.null(result)) return(tibble::tibble())
  tibble::as_tibble(result@result)
}

# Convert "a/b" ratio strings (GeneRatio, BgRatio) to numbers
ratio_to_numeric <- function(ratio) {
  stringr::str_split(ratio, "/") |>
    purrr::map_dbl(\(x) as.numeric(x[1]) / as.numeric(x[2]))
}
}
```

## Identify cutoffs

All four methods are written as "keep the top N genes," so we get N for each method and metaprogram first, then pull gene sets with the same function.

### Approach #1: Kneedle

Use the kneedle algorithm to identify the elbow using all positive weights as input

- Identify the elbow point for each metaprogram
- Make a table of the number of genes that are left above the elbow for each metaprogram

```{r}
kneedle_df <- filtered_weights_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(weight > 0) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    kneedle = find_kneedle_n(weight),
    total_pos_genes = dplyr::n_distinct(rank),
    .by = mp
  )

kneedle_df
```

I think that's way too many genes... 

```{r}
# Kneedle difference curve, optionally on just the top `max_genes` positive weights
calculate_difference_curve <- function(weights, max_genes = Inf) {
  positive_weights <- sort(weights[weights > 0], decreasing = TRUE) |>
    head(max_genes)
  n <- length(positive_weights)
  stopifnot("Need at least 3 positive weights to find an elbow" = n >= 3)

  x_norm <- (seq_len(n) - 1) / (n - 1)
  y_norm <- (positive_weights - min(positive_weights)) /
    (max(positive_weights) - min(positive_weights))
  (1 - x_norm) - y_norm
}

# Elbow = rank where the difference curve peaks
find_kneedle_n <- function(weights, max_genes = Inf) {
  calculate_difference_curve(weights, max_genes) |>
    which.max() |>
    unname() |>
    as.integer()
}

caps <- c(100, 150, 200, 300, 500)

kneedle_cap_df <- tidyr::expand_grid(mp = names(mp_list), max_genes = caps) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    kneedle = purrr::map2_int(mp, max_genes, \(m, cap) find_kneedle_n(mp_list[[m]], cap)),
    knee_strength = purrr::map2_dbl(mp, max_genes, \(m, cap) max(calculate_difference_curve(mp_list[[m]], cap)))
  )

kneedle_cap_df |>
  ggplot(aes(max_genes, kneedle, color = mp)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Kneedle input cap (top N positive genes)", y = "Elbow (number of genes kept)") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2")
```

```{r}
kneedle_cap_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(max_genes == 200)
```


### Approach #2: Outlier detection

Identify the number of genes that is 3 MADs outside the median gene weight to get outliers

- Identify the outliers for each metaprogram
- Make a table of the number of genes that are included when using the 3 MAD cutoff

```{r}
filtered_weights_df |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    mad_cutoff_weight = find_mad_cutoff(weight),
    mad_outliers = find_log_mad_n(weight),
    .by = "mp"
  )
```

### Cumulative weight cutoff 

```{r}
# Gini coefficient of positive weights (sorted ascending for the formula)
calculate_gini <- function(weights) {
  w <- sort(weights[weights > 0])
  n <- length(w)
  sum((2 * seq_len(n) - n - 1) * w) / (n * sum(w))
}

purrr::map_dbl(mp_list, calculate_gini)

```

```{r}
cumulative_weights_df <- filtered_weights_df |>
  dplyr::arrange(mp, rank) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cumulative_frac = cumsum(weight) / sum(weight), .by = mp)

cumulative_weights_df |>
  ggplot(aes(rank, cumulative_frac)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 200, color = "red") +  # current cutoff
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(vars(mp), scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Rank (log10)", y = "Cumulative fraction of positive weight")
```

```{r}
# Smallest N whose top genes capture at least `frac` of the total positive weight
find_cumulative_n <- function(weights, frac = 0.25) {
  positive_weights <- sort(weights[weights > 0], decreasing = TRUE)
  cumulative_frac <- cumsum(positive_weights) / sum(positive_weights)
  as.integer(which(cumulative_frac >= frac)[1])
}

tidyr::expand_grid(mp = names(mp_list), frac = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_genes = purrr::map2_int(mp, frac, \(m, f) find_cumulative_n(mp_list[[m]], f))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = frac, values_from = n_genes, names_prefix = "frac_")
```

## ORA 


```{r}
# Pull the top n genes by weight
# function to extract the top genes from each MP
# takes a list of named gene weight vectors and returns a list of gene id vectors,
# ordered by decreasing weight, with `num_genes` genes for each MP
extract_top_genes <- function(mp_list, num_genes){

  # get the top X number of genes for each MP
  mp_top_list <- mp_list |>
    purrr::map(function(weights){
      weights |>
        sort(decreasing = TRUE) |>
        head(n = num_genes) |>
        names() # return gene ids not weights
    })

  return(mp_top_list)
}

# function for running ORA with clusterProfiler::enricher on each metaprogram
# returns a df with all gene sets for each metaprogram with p.adjust <= 0.05
run_ora <- function(mp_top_list, gene_universe, term2gene_df){
  
  # run ORA using the top genes
  ora_results <- mp_top_list |> 
    purrr::map(\(genes){
      clusterProfiler::enricher(
        gene = genes,
        universe = gene_universe,
        TERM2GENE = term2gene_df
      )
    })
  
  # combine ora results into a single dataframe
  # only include genesets with pvalue < 0.05, the default by enricher 
  ora_results_df <- ora_results |> 
    purrr::map(\(ora) ora@result ) |> 
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "metaprogram") |>
    dplyr::filter(p.adjust <= 0.05) 
  
  return(ora_results_df)
  
}
```


